classification.difficultyReason: Build an exponential rule from doubling, then refine trial values around the half-minute boundary to justify nearest-minute rounding and express the exact time logarithmically.

content.prompt: A single bacterium cell divides into two every minute.

inlines.text: Start with 1 cell at 0 minutes and double each minute:

children.label: b
children.prompt: Write an equation for the population, $P$, after $t$ minutes.

answer.worked:
The initial population is 1 cell and doubles each minute.
$$\begin{align*}P&=1\times 2^t\\P&=2^t\end{align*}$$
$P$ is measured in cells and $t$ in minutes.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Use your rule to find the population after 8 minutes.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Using the exponential model, use trial and error to find the time (correct to the nearest minute) for the population to rise to 10000.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2^{13}&=8192\\2^{14}&=16384\\2^{13.5}&\approx11585\end{align*}$$
The model population increases with time. Since $8192<10000<11585$, the required time lies between 13 and 13.5 minutes, so it is 13 minutes to the nearest minute.
